prompt:
You are a strict medical pronunciation checker (North American English). Each audio file contains separate takes separated by 1.5 s of silence. The intended script of each take is given with its time range. For EACH take: check every medical word is pronounced correctly (correct sounds AND stress), that no word is skipped, garbled, or read as letters by mistake, and that the take is complete (nothing cut off at the start or end). Reply ONLY with a compact list: take id, PASS or FAIL, and for FAIL the exact word and how it actually sounded. Do not fail a take for an acceptable alternative pronunciation.

FILE w_cjd.wav:
cjd00 (0.0-6.2s): "Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is a rapidly progressive dementia caused by misfolded prion proteins."
cjd01 (7.7-14.6s): "Patients decline over weeks to months, with myoclonus, ataxia, and visual or behavioural change."
cjd02 (16.1-24.1s): "Diffusion MRI is the most sensitive test. Look for bright, restricted cortex that follows the gyri. That's cortical ribboning."
cjd03 (25.6-28.6s): "The caudate and putamen are often bright too."
cjd04 (30.1-39.3s): "In variant CJD, the pulvinar of the thalamus is brightest. That's the pulvinar sign. Add the dorsomedial thalamus, and you get the hockey stick sign."
cjd05 (40.8-47.3s): "Support the diagnosis with an RT-QuIC test on the CSF, and periodic sharp waves on EEG."
cjd06 (48.8-53.9s): "There's no cure, and most patients with sporadic CJD die within a year."
cjd07 (55.4-61.1s): "Rapid dementia with myoclonus, and bright cortex on diffusion? Think CJD."
Key words: Creutzfeldt-Jakob (KROYTS-felt YAH-kob); prion (PREE-on); myoclonus (my-oh-KLOH-nus); ataxia; caudate; putamen (pew-TAY-men); pulvinar (pul-VY-nar); dorsomedial; thalamus; RT-QuIC (R-T quick); C-J-D; E-E-G

FILE w_pres.wav:
pres00 (0.0-4.4s): "PRES stands for posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome."
pres01 (5.9-14.8s): "It's triggered by severe hypertension, eclampsia, kidney failure, and drugs like tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and chemotherapy."
pres02 (16.3-22.8s): "When blood pressure overwhelms autoregulation, fluid leaks out of the vessels. That's vasogenic edema."
pres03 (24.3-30.4s): "The back of the brain is most vulnerable, because the posterior circulation has less sympathetic protection."
pres04 (31.9-36.4s): "Patients present with headache, seizures, confusion, and visual loss."
pres05 (37.9-46.1s): "On FLAIR, look for symmetric bright signal in the parietal and occipital white matter and cortex. Diffusion is usually normal."
pres06 (47.6-53.9s): "Atypical cases involve the frontal lobes, cerebellum, or brainstem, and some bleed."
pres07 (55.4-60.3s): "Treat the cause and control the blood pressure. Most cases fully reverse."
pres08 (61.8-67.0s): "Hypertension, seizures, and bright posterior white matter? Think PRES."
Key words: PRES (said as the word press); posterior; encephalopathy (en-SEF-uh-LOP-uh-thee); eclampsia; tacrolimus (tak-ROH-lih-mus); cyclosporine (SY-kloh-SPOR-een); autoregulation; vasogenic (vay-zoh-JEN-ik); edema; sympathetic; parietal; occipital; cerebellum

FILE w_sih.wav:
sih00 (0.0-5.9s): "Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is caused by a CSF leak, usually in the spine."
sih01 (7.4-12.9s): "The classic symptom is an orthostatic headache. It's worse upright, and better lying down."
sih02 (14.4-20.4s): "As CSF is lost, the brain sags, and the veins and dura engorge to fill the space."
sih03 (21.9-30.9s): "Remember SEEPS. Subdural collections, enhancing pachymeninges, engorged veins, pituitary hyperemia, and sagging brain."
sih04 (32.4-41.1s): "On sagittal MRI, the brainstem sags, the cerebellar tonsils descend, and the space in front of the pons narrows."
sih05 (42.6-47.1s): "After contrast, the dura enhances smoothly and diffusely."
sih06 (48.6-52.6s): "Don't mistake the low tonsils for a Chiari malformation."
sih07 (54.1-59.1s): "Find the leak with spine imaging, then treat with an epidural blood patch."
sih08 (60.6-65.0s): "Orthostatic headache, and a sagging brain? Think CSF leak."
Key words: intracranial; hypotension; C-S-F; orthostatic; SEEPS (said as the word seeps); subdural; pachymeninges (pak-ee-meh-NIN-jeez); hyperemia (hy-per-EE-mee-uh); pituitary; sagittal; cerebellar tonsils; pons; dura; Chiari (kee-AR-ee); epidural
